transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-12
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Orion CTO), Priya Nair (Orion Sr Infra Eng), Evan Moore (Product)
notes: Call focused on Private VPC deployment options (VPC peering vs private endpoints), region constraints, and security/compliance needs.
raw_transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for taking the time today, uh this is maya and with me is liam from our se team.
[00:06] Raj (Orion CTO): thanks, maya, yeah we've been looking at redwood for about a month, trying to figure out hosted vs dedicated vs private. main ask is private because we need network isolation and keys staying in our account.
[00:18] Liam (Redwood SE): cool, yeah we'll go through the options. quick qualifier, can you share where your workloads live? region, VPC setup?
[00:24] Priya (Orion Sr Infra Eng): we're mostly in us-west-2, some services in eu-west-1 for GDPR workloads. primary concern is no public egress for inference traffic, and we want to use our KMS for key management.
[00:38] Maya: perfect. generally for private we offer two patterns: VPC peering/transit-gw with dedicated instances in your VPC, or private endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) to our control plane with inference traffic routed via private links. both have tradeoffs.
[00:52] Raj: i guess peering means the model runs in our VPC entirely? do we manage the GPUs?
[00:58] Liam: good question. with Redwood Private we can deploy the inference workers into your environment (we call it private deployment) — you provide the VPC and subnets, we deploy our runtime, but we still manage the software and updates. GPUs can be customer-managed if on-prem, but for cloud private we typically bring our images to your account and run on your instances — that lets you control the network and egress.
[01:20] Evan: is that similar to a dedicated host? how is this different from Redwood Dedicated offering?
[01:26] Maya: Dedicated is reserved capacity in our managed clusters; Private is full network isolation in your VPC and optionally in your account. Dedicated is easier to start, Private is for regulated workloads that need tighter controls.
[01:38] [01:40] Priya: about peering vs privatelink — we have a policy against transitive peering across multiple accounts, and we use a Transit Gateway. will that be a showstopper?
[01:47] Liam: not necessarily. we support Transit Gateway peering and can set up attachments; the common pattern is to host the inference VPC in your account and use TGW for routing. if you want private endpoints, we can front with PrivateLink but that means we keep the runtime in our account and expose endpoints into yours — some customers prefer that because it reduces operational burden.
[02:08] Raj: latency is a concern. we need sub-50ms p95 for short chat completions. can you meet that from us-west-2?
[02:15] Liam: depends on model size and token length; for smaller models and optimized runtime we typically see 20-40ms in-region. for larger context lengths the KV cache and batching affect latency. we'll run benchmarks but initial expectation is doable in us-west-2.
[02:31] Maya: also worth noting that PrivateLink option adds a small latency hit versus in-VPC deployment because of cross-account endpoints, maybe 5-15ms typical.
[02:40] [02:41] Priya: SOC2 and audit logs — we need audit trails for every inference request, retention for 13 months, and SSO via our IdP (Okta). do you support that?
[02:50] Liam: yes, audit logs are part of the platform — in Private we can ship logs to your S3/CloudWatch or to our control plane with forwarding. SSO/SAML with Okta and RBAC is supported. for keys, we integrate with customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS or HSM) so data plane encryption keys never leave your control.
[03:12] Raj: what's the networking setup for egress IPs — our egress policy whitelists specific IPs, we can't have dynamic ranges.
[03:20] Maya: for Private in your account, egress is controllable by you — the inference workers egress from your subnet so you can NAT to a fixed IP. for PrivateLink we publish a list of static endpoints but there's still some maintenance. we can provide an egress IP list for Dedicated/private endpoints as part of the onboarding docs.
[03:38] Evan: around quotas and autoscaling — if we put it in our VPC, how does autoscaling work? will redwood auto-scale instances in our account?
[03:45] Liam: yes, we can integrate with your autoscaling groups and our controller will scale up/down based on queue depth, but policy needs IAM permissions. we'll provide a terraform module to wire up ASG, IAM roles, and SSM for upgrades.
[03:58] [04:00] Priya: we also need private DNS, split-horizon. can the control plane resolve internal names?
[04:06] Liam: control plane traffic is optional to go over private link. if you want full private control plane in your VPC we have an option to run a private control plane (customer-managed control plane) — that requires extra ops but gives full DNS and internal-only communications. otherwise we use mTLS and mutual auth over PrivateLink.
[04:28] Raj: any limitations on regions? we can't run anything in certain countries, and some models need to be pinned to eu-west-1 for GDPR prod.
[04:35] Maya: we support us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1, and a handful of other regions. for EU-only workloads we can deploy in eu-west-1 and ensure data residency. private on-prem deployments are also possible for air-gapped requirements.
[04:52] [05:00] Evan: what about model versions and rollouts — if we pin a model, can we do canary within our VPC?
[05:06] Liam: yes, rollouts, canary, A/B tests are supported and the console/agent can handle traffic splitting at the route level. metrics and traces are exported to your telemetry stack or Redwood's console depending on config.
[05:20] Priya: security scans — we need to run vulnerability scans on images. do you provide scanned images or do we scan them ourselves?
[05:27] Liam: we provide hardened base images and a SBOM; customers can also run their own scanning. for Private we can arrange an image signing flow and CI integration so images are validated before runtime.
[05:40] [05:45] Raj: cost model — is Private priced differently? we want a sense of egress/cost per token and reserved capacity options.
[05:52] Maya: Private has licensing plus infra cost. for cloud private where you run instances in your account, you're billed for compute and storage on your side; Redwood charges a platform fee (per node or usage-based) plus support. Dedicated is more of a commit model with reserved monthly commits. we'll send pricing examples in the follow-up.
[06:10] Evan: also curious about quantization and perf — do you support INT8/4-bit to reduce instance sizes?
[06:15] Liam: yes, runtime supports quantized kernels and we recommend quant profiles per model. we'll include recommended profiles for their workload in the perf doc.
[06:24] Maya: quick question for Priya — do you have any blockers in terms of network topology, e.g., strict TGW routes or NO-PUBLIC-EGRESS rules?
[06:32] Priya: yes, our compliance DNS mandates no public endpoints for certain subnets and all egress must flow through their firewall. also we use a managed transit gw that disallows cross-account peering unless approved by netsec.
[06:45] Liam: okay that pushes us toward deploying the inference workers in your account and using TGW attachments. we can avoid cross-account peering.
[06:55] [07:00] Raj: about data retention and redaction — we send PHI-ish content, need to ensure logs are redacted or kept only in our S3.
[07:07] Liam: we can configure request/response logging to be stored only in your S3, and redact sensitive fields via a preprocessor. we'll document patterns — e.g., prefix hashing, tokenization — for PII removal.
[07:22] Maya: i'll add a sample terraform snippet for the S3 logging path and the KMS CMK policy.
[07:30] Evan: what's the typical onboarding timeline for Private?
[07:34] Maya: usually 4-8 weeks: discovery, network setup, small pilot (2-4 nodes), run benchmarks, then expand. if it's on-prem it can be longer due to procurement.
[07:45] [07:50] Priya: what telemetry do you need from our side to run benchmarks?
[07:53] Liam: we'll need representative prompts, expected concurrency, p95 latency targets, and traffic shapes. we'll also ask for sample payload sizes so we can model KV cache and sequence lengths.
[08:06] Raj: are there any known limitations with Transit Gateway attachments? e.g., MTU/fragmentation?
[08:12] Liam: generally no, but heavy throughput with very large payloads might need tuning. we recommend jumbo frames be consistent across routes. we'll include a networking checklist.
[08:23] Maya: i'm going to share a few docs in the chat: Private VPC runbook, architecture diagram, and a sample POc sheet.
[08:30] [08:35] Priya: please include a list of required IAM roles and least-privilege policies.
[08:38] Liam: yes our terraform module is least-privilege by default and we can share it.
[08:44] Evan: about failover — if a region goes down, can we route to another region? how does data jurisdiction work?
[08:51] Maya: we support cross-region failover but you need to plan for data residency. for EU-only data we can keep backups in eu-west-1 and failover within EU. cross-region failover requires replication configs.
[09:03] [09:10] Raj: for the pilot we'll start small: 2 nodes in us-west-2 with a 1-week benchmark window. we'd like to test latency and cost per 1M tokens.
[09:18] Maya: sounds good. liam will draft the perf plan and we will run a bench with your sample prompts.
[09:24] Priya: one last networking question — can your agents run inside our private subnets with no outbound internet at all?
[09:31] Liam: yes, if you give us egress via your NAT or a proxy; our updater uses SSM or a pull model over a private endpoint. for fully air-gapped we have an on-prem package but it requires extra setup.
[09:45] [09:50] Evan: competitors — have you seen customers switch from Anthropic or OpenAI for similar reasons?
[09:55] Maya: yes, some customers moved from hosted Anthropic/OpenAI to private deployments for compliance and cost. we also get comparisons to self-hosted open models; our differentiation is the runtime optimizations and operator experience.
[10:06] Liam: for the benchmark plan we'll look at both quantized and fp16 profiles and recommend instance families (g5/g5n style or equivalent) for throughput/latency tradeoffs.
[10:18] Maya: wrap-up, recap of next steps: we'll send the doc pack, liam will draft the perf plan and pricing, priya will share VPC details and firewall constraints, and we'll schedule the networking deep-dive next week.
[10:32] Raj: thanks all, appreciate the clarity.
[10:36] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with the links (Private VPC runbook: https://redwood.ai/docs/private-vpc and POc sheet: https://drive.google.com/example-orion-poc).
[10:45] END OF TRANSCRIPT
